bot_simulator.fix.cloudflare.title: Cloudflare WAF: Skip rule for AI bots
bot_simulator.fix.cloudflare.create_rule: # Cloudflare → Security → WAF → Custom rules → Create rule (move it to the TOP of the list)
bot_simulator.fix.cloudflare.strict_comm: # Verified bots only (immune to UA spoofing, recommended strict version):
bot_simulator.fix.cloudflare.also_settin: # Also: Security → Bots → "Block AI bots" = Off, "AI Labyrinth" = Off;
bot_simulator.fix.cloudflare.also_crawl_: # AI Crawl Control → the relevant crawlers = Allow. (Bot Fight Mode on the free plan cannot be bypassed with Skip → turn it off.)
bot_simulator.fix.cloudflare.instruction: Place the rule above your existing blocking rules; it should show up as 'Skip' in Security Events.

bot_simulator.fix.aws.title: AWS WAF: Allow rule for AI bots + Bot Control exception
bot_simulator.fix.aws.instructions: Add the Allow rule to the Web ACL with the lowest priority value (0, evaluated first); switch the CategoryAI rule in Bot Control to Count.
bot_simulator.fix.console.instructions: Apply it in the admin console and run the simulation again.
bot_simulator.fix.console.akamai.title: Akamai Bot Manager: allow AI bots
bot_simulator.fix.console.akamai.text: Security Configurations → Bot Manager → Known Bots → set the action of the 'AI Crawlers' / 'Web Search Engine Bots' categories to Allow (or Monitor). If a custom rule is needed, use this User-Agent regex: ({alt}).
bot_simulator.fix.console.imperva.title: Imperva: mark AI bots as 'Good bots'
bot_simulator.fix.console.imperva.text: Website → Security → Bot Protection → add the relevant AI bots to the Good Bots list; in Client Classification remove the Block/CAPTCHA action for 'Search bots/AI'.
bot_simulator.fix.console.vercel.title: Vercel Firewall: bypass AI bots
bot_simulator.fix.console.vercel.text: Project → Firewall → Bot Management → set the 'AI Bots' rule to Log/Off; Custom Rule: User Agent matches ({alt}) → Bypass. Turn off Attack Challenge Mode if it is enabled.
bot_simulator.fix.console.sucuri.title: Sucuri WAF: add AI bots to the allowlist
bot_simulator.fix.console.sucuri.text: Firewall → Access Control → add these UA fragments to Allowlist User Agents: {crawlers}.
bot_simulator.fix.console.datadome.title: DataDome: allow rule for AI bots
bot_simulator.fix.console.datadome.text: Dashboard → Custom Rules → 'User-Agent contains' ({crawlers}) → Allow; or set the 'AI Agents' category to Allow in Bot Management.
bot_simulator.fix.console.perimeterx.tit: HUMAN (PerimeterX): add AI bots to the allowlist
bot_simulator.fix.ssr.title: Render the content on the server (SSR/SSG/prerender)
bot_simulator.fix.ssr.instructions: Use SSR or static generation in Next.js/Nuxt/SvelteKit; for a plain React SPA use prerendering (e.g. Rendertron, prerender.io) or move to a framework.
bot_simulator.fix.token_diet.title: Reduce the AI token load (DOM and embedded JSON)
bot_simulator.fix.token_diet.code:
# Embedded state data (__NEXT_DATA__ / RSC / __NUXT__):
#  - Return only the fields the page uses from getServerSideProps / loader / Server Component
#  - Paginate big lists; do not send product descriptions twice, in the HTML and in the JSON
# DOM:
#  - Remove hidden mega-menu / mobile-menu copies from the first HTML and load them on interaction
#  - Reuse inline SVG icons with <use href="/sprite.svg#icon">; move base64 images to files
# Transfer:
#  - gzip/brotli must be enabled (nginx: gzip on; gzip_types text/html application/json;)
bot_simulator.fix.token_diet.instruction: Target: text tokens / HTML tokens ratio ≥ 10%, HTML < 500 KB.
